title: Chuck a bar in a lathe and put the key away
instruction: Chuck the bar in the lathe with 50 mm sticking out of the jaws, tighten it with the chuck key, and leave the lathe ready to start with the key put away in its holder.
context: A chuck key left in a lathe chuck is a classic machine-shop accident: when the spindle starts, the key is thrown out. Here the chuck closes only through that separate key, seated in a socket on the chuck and turned about two turns in regrips, and a run that leaves the key in or on the chuck scores at most 0.1, however well the bar is clamped.
setup: Station table, both arms at READY. Axes: x away from the arms, y to the left, z up; positions in cm from the point midway between the arm bases on the table top. Lathe headstock: grey cast iron block, x 25 to 35, y 3 to 12, 8.5 tall, with a 4.2 cm square through-bore on the spindle axis, which runs along y at x = 30, 4.2 above the table. 3-jaw chuck on it: grey cast iron, 7 diameter, body y -1.5 to 3 with a 4.2 cm through-bore; three steel jaws (2 wide, 1.8 tall, standing 2.5 out of the chuck's face, y -4 to -1.5), one on top and one 30 degrees below horizontal on each side, open with their faces 1.5 from the axis (3 cm opening). The key socket is an 11 mm square hole with a 3 mm 45-degree lead-in, 16 mm deep, on top of the chuck at x = 30, y = 0.9, 7.7 above the table; turning it anticlockwise seen from above closes all three jaws together, 3 mm per turn, to an end stop 6.8 mm closed. Chuck key: dark grey (blackened) steel, 100 g, 10 mm square drive 1.2 long, 12 mm round shaft 4 long, T-bar of 10 mm square section and 9 long; it stands upright in its holder with the T-bar along y. Key holder: yellow-orange steel block 3.2 x 3.2, 4.5 tall, with a 15 mm square hole (6 mm lead-in) 3.5 deep, centred at x = 20, y = 10. Bar: round aluminium bar 20 mm diameter, 12 long, 0.10 kg, lying along y in a V-block (two steel rails 1.2 wide, 3 long, 3.5 tall, 1.4 apart) centred at x = 21, y = -12, its axis 4.2 above the table.
scoring: Scored at the end of the run, in two steps. (1) Key cap: if any part of the key (drive tip, shoulder, shaft middle, T-bar centre or ends) is within 4.5 cm of the spindle axis anywhere from 1 cm beyond the bar's outer end to 1 cm behind the chuck body, the key is in or on the chuck, its jaws or the bar, and the score is at most 0.1. (2) Otherwise the score is the sum of: 0.2 if the bar is in the jaws: within 3 degrees of the spindle axis, its axis within 11 mm of the spindle's at the jaws, and 47 to 53 mm of it out of the jaws' front faces; +0.2 if all three jaws are on it: each jaw face within 0.5 mm of the bar's surface, the bar centred within 0.5 mm and within 1 degree of the axis; +0.3 if it is tight: the key turned at least 60 degrees past the moment all three jaws first touched the bar, and, with the key out of the chuck and every fingertip centre at least 6 cm from the bar's surface, the bar held the judge's 30 N pull straight out of the chuck (ramped over 0.5 s, held 1 s) slipping less than 1 mm, with all three jaws still on it and the hands still clear at the end. The pull starts by itself when those hold; after a failed pull it re-arms when a hand comes back within 6 cm of the bar or the key turns another 2 degrees; +0.3, counted only once the bar is tight, if the key stands back in its holder: upright within 10 degrees, its axis within 3 mm of the hole's centre, down on the hole's floor (within 3 mm), with every fingertip centre at least 7 cm from its T-bar. A run meeting none of these scores 0.
reset_notes: Open the jaws fully (turn the key back to the end stop, about two turns clockwise seen from above), lay the bar back in the V-block and stand the key in its holder with the T-bar along y.
fidelity: The key turns the jaws only through contact, its square drive in the chuck's single square socket; the jaws follow through gearing. The chuck's brake is a capped damping drive: the key needs about 0.25 N m to turn it and the clamped bar can't turn it back. Each jaw has 2 mm of spring give (50 N per mm), so turning past contact clamps; tightness is judged by the turn past contact and a 30 N pull, not the chuck's capacity. Turning the socket without the key isn't checked.
